title: Meaning from local context
summary: Use definitions, examples, contrast, cause and tone around an unfamiliar word to test its likely meaning instead of guessing from the word alone.

sections.title: Start with evidence
content: Read: “The room was dim, with only one weak lamp in the corner.” Which nearby words explain dim?
Name the clue, then state the likely meaning. The aim is to practise pointing to evidence before choosing an answer.

sections.title: Five useful context clues
content: A definition restates the meaning, often after a dash, comma or colon.
An example shows actions or objects that share the meaning.
A contrast uses signals such as unlike, although, but or however.
A cause or result shows what the word makes happen.
The tone combines the situation and the writer’s attitude.
Use a three-step routine: identify the clue, predict a simple meaning, then test every option in the original sentence.

sections.title: Why a plausible distractor can still fail
content: In “The slope was treacherous—dangerous and unstable after the rain,” the dash introduces a direct definition.
“Narrow” may describe some difficult paths, but it is unsupported here. “Hazardous” matches both dangerous and unstable.
A correct option must fit the actual sentence, not merely the general topic.

sections.title: Name the clue before answering
content: Complete two items with a clue prompt. After each response, compare every option with the words that carry the evidence.

sections.title: Apply the routine independently
content: For each unseen sentence, write a two- or three-word prediction before inspecting the options. Choose the option only after testing it in the sentence.

sections.title: Diagnose the mistake
content: Unknown meaning: the word and clues were both unfamiliar.
Missed clue: useful evidence was present but overlooked.
Option trap: an option matched the topic but not the sentence.
Tone mismatch: the basic meaning fit but the feeling or strength did not.
Record one category and one action for the retry.

sections.title: Transfer to a new sentence
content: Complete one unseen item without a clue label. A correct answer demonstrates the context routine on a fresh word; an error enters the retry queue with the recorded error category.
